cards.b: Content, Form, Process, Mood: a framework for analysing any artwork.
The subject matter and meaning of an artwork.
The visual elements and how they are arranged: line, tone, colour, texture, shape, composition.
The materials, techniques and tools used to make the work.
The feeling or atmosphere created, and how.
Short written notes beside your work: what you did, why, what you learned, what next.

cards.f: Three parts of annotating your own work
cards.b: What I did; what happened/what I notice; what I will do next.

cards.f: Which AO does reflection support most?
cards.b: AO2: refining work driven by insights from exploring ideas and reflection. Also AO3 and AO1.
nice, good, interesting, detailed: they say nothing specific.
Thick paint applied so brushstrokes stand out from the surface, as in Van Gogh.
Strong contrast of light and dark to create drama and a sense of form.
Colours opposite each other on the colour wheel, such as blue and orange.
The part of a composition the eye is drawn to first.
Picasso, 1937: black, white and grey oil painting about the bombing of Guernica; hangs in the Reina Sofía, Madrid.

gaps.s: The four parts of CFPM are content, form, process and ___.
The L in PEEL stands for ___.
Thick paint that stands out from the surface is called ___.
Annotation should be placed ___ the work it describes.
Strong contrast between light and dark is called ___.
Saying what you will do next shows a ___ decision.

short.q: Write a PEEL analysis (3-4 sentences) of a work you know.
short.model: E.g. Van Gogh's brushstrokes in The Starry Night swirl; the thick impasto catches light; this makes the sky restless; I will use directional marks in my own study.

short.q: Explain why 'It looks nice' earns no marks.
short.model: It is vague: no description of how it is made, no analysis of effect and no link to the student's own work.

short.q: Analyse the mood of Guernica using two formal elements.
short.model: The limited black, white and grey palette and the sharp, fragmented shapes create a mood of horror and chaos.

short.q: Give two sentence starters that show evaluation.
short.model: 'This was successful because…' and 'It did not work as I hoped because…'.

short.q: Why should annotation be next to the work?
short.model: It makes the link between the writing and the evidence clear and is easy for the examiner to read.
